prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Katy, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1161; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the recording, but I can confirm I'm the driver of the vehicle involved in the collision.

Q: That's fine. Can you walk me through what happened at the intersection in Katy?

A: I was heading through on the green light, moving at a normal speed. A pickup coming from my right ran the red and hit the side of my car. I didn't see him until he was already in the intersection.

Q: Did you have any chance to brake or swerve before impact?

A: Maybe a second. I hit the brakes, but there wasn't time to do much else.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, and I think that's the only reason I'm not in worse shape. The belt locked up hard across my chest and my shoulder.

Q: Where are you feeling pain now?

A: Mostly in the lower back, on the left side. It's a deep ache, and it gets sharp when I bend or lift anything. Sitting in the car for long periods makes it worse.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or gone to urgent care?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic that afternoon. They checked my range of motion, took some X-rays, and said it looked like a muscle strain. They gave me a muscle relaxer and told me to follow up with my primary care physician if it doesn't improve.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?

A: A couple of shifts so far. I'm doing what I can at a desk, but lifting is out of the question right now.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Only that I was following the rules of the road, and I'd like to make sure my medical bills get handled properly.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
